summary: Space Explorer is an interactive, browser-based space mission design and simulation game developed to make complex space engineering concepts understandable through practical experimentation. Players can select destinations such as the Moon, Mars and Europa, configure spacecraft using different components, and make engineering decisions while managing limited resources such as budget, mass, power and propulsion requirements. The game addresses the challenge of understanding the interdependence of spacecraft systems by demonstrating how each engineering decision influences overall mission feasibility and performance. Through dynamic resource calculations, mission readiness checks and simulated space travel, users can experiment with different spacecraft configurations and learn from their decisions. It also features a Mars rover exploration environment where players can deploy a rover, manage its battery and complete scientific objectives. By transforming theoretical aerospace concepts into an interactive learning experience, the project encourages scientific curiosity, engineering problem-solving and interest in future space exploration.
details:
Space Explorer provides an interactive environment that takes users through different stages of a simulated space mission, from selecting a planetary destination to spacecraft assembly, launch preparation, simulated travel and planetary exploration. Players can choose between three mission scenarios: Lunar Recon, Ares Vanguard and Europa Clipper. They can assemble their spacecraft by selecting different components, including core modules, propulsion systems and power systems. Each component has predefined engineering characteristics, and the game dynamically calculates the spacecraft's total mass, budget, power generation, power consumption and estimated delta-v. A mission readiness system evaluates whether the selected spacecraft meets its predefined requirements before allowing the player to proceed.

Following successful mission preparation, users can experience simulated space travel and encounter unexpected mission events. The Mars mission also includes a dedicated surface exploration simulator where players can deploy and control a rover, explore the Martian surface, monitor battery consumption and complete scientific objectives. Mission progress can be saved locally in the browser.

The project combines engineering concepts, simulation and game-based learning to help users understand spacecraft systems, resource management and the consequences of engineering decisions. It encourages critical thinking, experimentation, decision-making and problem-solving while making aerospace concepts approachable for students and beginners. Its intended impact is to bridge the gap between theoretical space science and practical engineering understanding, inspiring more students to explore aerospace engineering, planetary science and future space technologies.

Developed as a software-based web application, the project uses HTML, CSS and JavaScript for its structure, interface and interactive game logic. Tailwind CSSis used for interface styling, while Google Fonts provides typography. Browser LocalStorage is used to save and restore mission progress locally. GitHub is used for source-code management and GitHub Pages for website hosting. No specialised hardware or dedicated backend server is required.

The innovative aspect of the project lies in combining spacecraft configuration, engineering trade-offs, mission simulation and planetary rover exploration into one interactive learning experience. Rather than presenting individual engineering concepts separately, it demonstrates how different spacecraft systems work together and how a decision in one area can influence the overall mission. Accessibility and affordability were considered by making the game browser-based, eliminating the need for specialised hardware or dedicated software installation. Standard web technologies and static hosting also help minimise development and operational costs. Energy management is incorporated into the gameplay through spacecraft power-generation and consumption calculations, as well as rover battery management. These features provide an engaging way to understand the importance of balancing engineering requirements and limited resources during space mission design.
